newsitem.title: USA: One dead as children's tour bus crashes in Virginia.
newsitem.headline: One dead as children's tour bus crashes in Virginia.

text.p: A youth was killed and several people were seriously injured when a bus carrying children on tour of the slavery-era "underground railroad" veered off Interstate 95 into the Nottoway River near Stony Creek, Virginia, on Tuesday, police said.
The bus, which was heading north, ended up half-submerged in the river, State Police spokeswoman Tammy VanDame said.

"We have one confirmed fatality in this accident and I'm not releasing any names. We don't know how many people were injured yet, she said. "The majority of the injuries were minor although we do have some life-threatening injuries."
The bus was carrying six chaperones and 29 students aged from 12 to 17 from all across the United States and the Bahamas on a tour called "Pathways to Freedom".

The tour, an educational program sponsored by the U.S. Department of Transportation, Shoney's Restaurants and civil rights leader Rosa Parks, retraces the underground railroad route taken by black slaves escaping the southern states for freedom in the north.
This leg of the tour was from Charleston, South Carolina, to Washington.
